concepts.title: Respiratory Organs and the Human Respiratory System
concepts.definition: Respiration occurs through body surface, tracheal system, gills or lungs depending on the animal; the human respiratory system includes external nostrils, nasal passage, pharynx, larynx with sound box, trachea, bronchi, bronchioles and alveoli surrounded by blood capillaries, with the lungs covered by pleural membranes.
concepts.key_idea: The alveoli, with their thin squamous epithelium and dense capillary network, are the primary sites of exchange of gases, while the conducting part only transports the air.

concepts.title: Respiratory Volumes and Capacities
concepts.definition: Breathing volumes include tidal volume of about 500 ml, inspiratory reserve volume, expiratory reserve volume and residual volume, and capacities combine them: inspiratory capacity equals tidal volume plus IRV, vital capacity equals IRV plus tidal volume plus ERV, and total lung capacity equals vital capacity plus residual volume.
concepts.key_idea: Intrapulmonary pressure falls below atmospheric pressure during inspiration as the diaphragm and external intercostals contract, and expiration is largely a passive return.

solution_steps.explain: Add inspiratory reserve, tidal volume and expiratory reserve to get the vital capacity

solution_steps.explain: Add the residual volume to the vital capacity to get the total lung capacity

concepts.title: Exchange and Transport of Gases
concepts.section: 14.4 Exchange of Gases, 14.5 Transport of Gases
concepts.definition: Oxygen and carbon dioxide exchange by pressure gradient across alveolar and tissue membranes; oxygen is transported mainly as oxyhaemoglobin, carbon dioxide mostly as bicarbonate formed under the enzyme carbonic anhydrase, and every 100 ml of deoxygenated blood delivers about 4 ml of carbon dioxide to the alveoli.
concepts.key_idea: The oxygen dissociation curve is sigmoid, and its shift to the right with higher carbon dioxide, hydrogen ion and temperature is the Bohr effect that favours unloading in tissues.

concepts.title: Regulation of Respiration and Respiratory Disorders
concepts.section: 14.6 Regulation of Respiration, 14.7 Disorders of Respiratory System
concepts.definition: Breathing is regulated by the respiratory rhythm centre in the medulla, the pneumotaxic centre in the pons and chemosensitive areas sensing carbon dioxide and hydrogen ions; disorders include asthma with bronchial constriction, emphysema with alveolar damage, and occupational respiratory disorders like asbestosis and silicosis.
concepts.key_idea: Carbon dioxide acts as the major stimulus for breathing through chemosensors, since oxygen plays only a minor role in normal regulation.
